genre: Taiwanese Mandarin narrative hip-hop with introspective urban rap storytelling
era_or_scene: late-night Taipei office-worker headphone music, polished but intimate, adult streaming-era rap production
mood: ambitious, exhausted, reflective, restrained, quietly cinematic, urban, emotionally mature
instrumentation: Rhodes electric piano with old business hotel texture
woody snare without trap electronic bite
simple 16th-note hi-hats with rare subtle rolls
soft subway-like 808/sub bass that vibrates without dominating
light pad lift in the hook
subtle airport ambience recreated with soft announcement-like texture, suitcase wheel feel, elevator ding, air-conditioning tone
very light strings only for the emotional lift
groove: 88 BPM head-nodding narrative rap groove, not trap, not drill, not emo rap; walking pace, steady and thoughtful, with lots of negative space
vocal_style: Traditional Chinese Mandarin spoken-rap delivery, almost conversational in the verses, no autotune, light compression and tape saturation, restrained hook that is half-rap half-melodic
arrangement: Intro with soft airport-like ambience and Rhodes. Verse stays sparse and office-at-midnight visual. First hook rises only slightly and leaves blank space. Bridge removes drums and keeps Rhodes plus airplane-engine-like ambience. Final hook lifts emotionally with light strings and stacked female ooh harmony without becoming loud. Outro strips back to engine ambience, Rhodes and low bass, ending with spoken self-talk.
section_focus: a 30-second proof-of-style clip covering the intro into the first hook: soft Gate B28 ambience, Rhodes Fm9-Ebmaj7-Dbmaj7-C7 loop, restrained 88 BPM drums, Taiwanese Mandarin spoken-rap texture, and a minimal hook lift around the phrase 下一班飛機 / 飛去哪裡 without copying any existing melody
production_texture: clean Spotify-ready mix, warm Rhodes, dry intimate rap vocal, subtle tape saturation, controlled low end, no harsh trap hats, no glossy EDM build, lots of empty space, cinematic late-night transit atmosphere
lyric_direction: Use Chinese characters only for vocals. Do not translate to English. Do not use pinyin. Keep lyrics original and close to the Gate B28 theme: ambition, waiting, transfer, office fatigue, not knowing whether moving forward is growth or escape.
avoid: do not imitate any named artist voice, cadence, flow, beat, or melody
do not make trap, drill, emo rap, TikTok hi-hat music, Future-style 808, or Travis Scott-style atmosphere
do not use generic airport stock sound effects too literally
do not use obvious piano ballad tropes
do not make the first hook explode
do not translate Chinese lyrics into English
do not copy melody, lyrics, hook, artist voice, or arrangement signature
